steps: Hook your dominant index finger over your thumb to form an X handshape, folding the remaining fingers down.
Place the hooked X hand just under your chin, close to the front of your throat.
Flick the X hand forward about three inches with a quick wrist motion, then repeat the flick once more.
Angle your palm slightly downward so the hooked X points forward as it slides away from your throat.
Hold a neutral, matter-of-fact expression — this sign simply names the material.
tip: The same flicking X also signs steel — it covers the whole metal family.

steps: Extend the index fingers of both hands, folding the remaining fingers of each hand into loose fists.
Hold your non-dominant index finger sideways at chest height, pointing across your body like the bottom bar of a plus sign.
Cross your dominant index finger over it at a right angle, touching the fingers near their middles to draw a plus.
Keep both palms facing each other as the fingertips meet at the center of the cross.
Wear a calm, upbeat expression that matches the meaning of staying positive.
tip: This is the math-class PLUS sign doing double duty — picture adding a plus to your attitude.

steps: Spread the fingers of both hands wide into open five handshapes.
Raise both hands to chest height in front of you, with all the fingers pointing upward.
Push the hands together so the fingertips interlock, like two opposing scrimmage lines clashing at the snap.
Ram the hands together twice in a quick double movement, keeping the fingers meshed.
Keep the palms facing each other through both rams of the sign.
Hold a neutral, game-ready expression — the double clash is part of the sign.
tip: The fingers are the two scrimmage lines, not a ball — never shape the hands into a football.

steps: Curve the fingers of both hands into loose bent handshapes, with the fingertips pointing downward.
Raise both bent hands to the tops of your shoulders, close to your neck.
Touch the fingertips down onto your shoulders, then lift and touch again with a firm double tap.
Keep the palms angled inward toward your chest through both contacts.
Hold a steady, earnest expression — the repeated tap marks this as a duty.
tip: No R handshape needed — think of the weight of a duty resting on your shoulders.

steps: Pinch your thumb and index finger together with the other fingers folded to form the letter G, palm facing you.
Open into U by extending your index and middle fingers straight up together.
Curl all four fingertips down onto your thumb to form E, keeping your palm facing forward.
Close your hand into an S fist with your thumb lying across the front of your folded fingers.
Finish with T by tucking your thumb up between your index and middle fingers, flowing smoothly between letters.
Hold your hand at chest height and mouth the word 'guest' lightly as you spell.
tip: Signers fingerspell the word itself — then use invite or visit to show what the guest is doing.
